name: diagnose
description: Run a disciplined diagnosis loop for hard bugs: reproduce, hypothesize, instrument, fix, regression-test.

steps.name: Establish feedback loop
steps.instruction: Set up the fastest possible feedback loop. Find or create the minimal reproduction path. Target: under 30 seconds from change to observed result.

steps.name: Reproduce the bug
steps.instruction: Reproduce the bug in an E2E setting as closely aligned with how an end user would encounter it. Write a failing test that captures the bug. If the bug can't be reproduced, document what was tried and escalate.

steps.name: Form hypothesis
steps.instruction: Form a specific, falsifiable hypothesis about the root cause. Write it down. Do not start fixing until the hypothesis is tested. Apply loop budget from routing policy: two evidence-producing repair attempts per failure fingerprint, then one bounded diagnostic pass.
checklist: Hypothesis distinguishes this bug from similar-looking bugs
Loop budget tracked per failure fingerprint

steps.name: Instrument and verify
steps.instruction: Add instrumentation to test the hypothesis. Logging, breakpoints, assertions. Observe the actual behavior. Confirm or reject the hypothesis. If rejected, form a new one.
checklist: Each attempt is evidence-producing (not speculative rewrite or blind retry)

steps.name: Fix
steps.instruction: Fix the root cause. The previously-failing test must now pass. Run the full test suite to check for regressions. Remove instrumentation.
checklist: Fix applied to root cause (not symptoms)

steps.name: Cleanup
steps.instruction: Clean up the fix. Ensure the test is well-named and documents the bug scenario. Remove any temporary code.
checklist: Test is well-named and documents the scenario

steps.name: Learn
steps.instruction: What caused this bug to be possible? Is there a class of similar bugs? Could a convention test or structural check prevent recurrence? If so, offer to create one.

tone: Methodical. Hypothesis first, fix second. No shotgun debugging.
